newsitem.title: FRANCE: Quality fears stifle French domestic grain market.
newsitem.headline: Quality fears stifle French domestic grain market.

text.p: Uncertainty over the quality of the harvest blocked most French wheat and barley business as the new European Union export season got under way on Thursday.
Standard Rouen-delivered wheat was nominally quoted at 855 to 860 francs a tonne for delivery spread over four months from September, traders said.
Those levels were unchanged after the EU granted just over 100,000 tonnes for export at its first 1997/98 tender.
"The market did not budge. There was not enough volume to force it to move," one trader said.
Instead traders focused on the problems of locking up supplies of best milling wheat in a year when feed is expected to dominate a large but possibly mediocre French crop.
Buyers were said to be offering premiums of at least 20 francs for guaranteed best-quality wheat but no one was prepared to offer such guarantees and no deals were done, brokers said.
For feed barley delivered into Dunkirk, firm buyers were reported at 840 francs for periods between August and December, also unchanged from the previous day.
Old-crop maize slipped five francs in southwest France as sellers there also started fretting about the likelihood of heavy supplies of competing feed wheat this year.
The weather in France's largest maize region has also been ideal, with alternating heat and moisture.
Fob Atlantic maize changed hands on Thursday at 837.50 francs a tonne.
New crop maize traded at the previous day's offered price of 880 francs a tonne, to the market's only buyer, for any period between October and June, brokers said.
In futures, Matif fob barge milling wheat rose six francs for February to 923 francs on contract volume of 53 lots. May rose seven to 935 with 11 lots.
Earlier positions were untraded.

French domestic cash grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
For 1997/98, the charges are currently as follows (francs per tonne).
